Over nearly five decades the Islamic Republic has shown that it is neither reformable nor willing to change its repressive nature. The structure of this regime rests on domestic repression, exporting crises, threatening regional security and confronting international order and security.

A large part of the insecurity, crisis and instability in the region originates in the policies of the Islamic Republic. Lasting freedom and security in the world will not be achievable without freeing Iran from the rule of this system.

We have concrete demands of your governments:

1. End appeasement: stop the policy of appeasement and concessions to the Islamic Republic and take a firm stance against the repression of the Iranian people.

2. Recognise Reza Pahlavi: recognise him in your political engagements as the central figure of the monarchist opposition and the political representative of Iran's monarchist movement.

3. Hand over the Islamic Republic's embassies: refrain from legitimising the regime's diplomatic missions, and, within the framework of international law, prepare the ground for transferring the management and control of Iran's diplomatic missions abroad to representatives approved by the Iranian people and the office of Prince Reza Pahlavi.

4. Support the transition: support transition-period plans and organised efforts for a peaceful transfer of power to the Iranian people.

5. Support the Iranian people: take practical action to stop executions, free political prisoners, counter repression and secure Iranians' free access to the internet.

6. Respect Iran's territorial integrity: support the right of the Iranian people to determine the future political system of their country through free and democratic elections.

We want a free, secular, united and prosperous Iran - an Iran in which the Pahlavi monarchy can become the country's political system by the free vote of the people.

We believe the bond between the Iranian nation and Reza Shah II Pahlavi, and the ideal of a return to national sovereignty, is one of the political paths supported by a large part of Iran's monarchist community.

This letter is not a request for interference in determining Iran's fate; it is a request to respect Iranians' right to determine their own fate.

We ask you not to see history through the lens of short-term political interests. A free Iran will be not a threat to the world but an opportunity for peace, stability and international cooperation.

The time has come to end appeasement and to hear the voice of the Iranian nation.

Long live Iran

Javid Shah

Anti-government demonstrations in Abdanan with chants in support of the Pahlavi family; a number of citizens arrested

- On Tuesday 26 Aban 1405, on the sidelines of the funeral for the victims of the deadly overturning of a bus carrying workers of the "NGL" company in Dehloran, Ilam province, which happened on the evening of Saturday 23 Aban, the people of Abdanan staged a protest. Protesters chanted against the system and voiced support for Prince Reza Pahlavi.

- Security forces and Basijis used tear gas and batons to disperse the crowd and the protests turned violent. Local sources said six people - Sina Darvishi (15 years old), Behnam Moradi, Mohsen Bavir, Iraj Heydari, Saeed Abdollahi and Asghar Akbari - were arrested by security forces.

- In these protests people chanted slogans against Khomeini and Khamenei and voiced support for the Pahlavi family. Among the chants were "Islamic Republic, where is your cartoon leader?", [a vulgar Lori-dialect chant insulting Khomeini], "The Islamic Republic must be destroyed", "Death to the dictator", "Javid Shah" and "This is the final battle, Pahlavi will return". People also set fire to an Islamic Republic flag and tore down a Basij banner.

- Prince Reza Pahlavi, in a message expressing sympathy with the families of the bus-crash victims, told the people of Abdanan: "Your courage is admirable, and the crimes of the Islamic Republic have not been able to weaken your will."

https://t.co/N6PfddyRdF
virals.note: Persian news report; English is a full translation. Names of detainees and the Crown Prince quote are as reported by Kayhan London; one vulgar chant is paraphrased.

outsiders.name: The Iran Watcher
outsiders.hook:
A senior IRGC commander has admitted that Israel can track regime officials through surveillance cameras, medical records, fuel purchases and airline bookings—leaving them nowhere to hide.

Brigadier General Mohammad Jafar Asadi warned that hostile intelligence services no longer depend solely on mobile phones to track the Islamic Republic’s officials and military personnel.

Surveillance cameras in streets, shops and homes feed information into artificial-intelligence systems. Medical visits, prescriptions, fuel purchases and airline tickets all create permanent digital records.

“In every place you go, your information trail remains in the systems,” Asadi said. “It can no longer be said that there is anywhere left to hide.”

This is not an outside analyst describing the regime’s vulnerability. Asadi is a former IRGC Ground Forces commander and former deputy inspector of the Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters.

His warning reflects how Israel repeatedly penetrated the Islamic Republic and Hezbollah.

Israel hacked nearly the entire traffic-camera network in Iran’s capital years before the strike that killed Ali Khamenei. Camera feeds were encrypted and transmitted to servers in Israel, allowing intelligence analysts to study the movements of senior officials and their security details.

One camera showed where Khamenei’s bodyguards parked their vehicles.

Algorithms then helped construct detailed “pattern-of-life” profiles: their addresses, schedules, travel routes and the officials they protected.

Combined with penetrated mobile networks, human sources and disrupted cellular service, this surveillance helped confirm that Khamenei and other senior officials were gathered at the leadership compound before it was struck.

The regime knew its cameras were compromised but failed to secure them.

In September 2025, senior parliamentarian Mahmoud Nabavian acknowledged that Israel controlled the cameras at Iran’s intersections and could detect the movement of officials through compromised internet-connected systems.

The irony is devastating.

The Islamic Republic built an enormous surveillance network to identify protesters, track dissidents and punish women for refusing compulsory hijab. Israel then turned that same machinery into a targeting system against the regime’s leadership.

The same intelligence doctrine shattered Hezbollah.

Israel combined signals interception, human sources, persistent aerial surveillance, data analysis and supply-chain penetration. The compromised pager and radio operation incapacitated thousands of Hezbollah personnel, disrupted communications and helped prepare the ground for the destruction of command centres and the killing of senior leaders, including Hassan Nasrallah.

Hezbollah tried abandoning mobile phones for supposedly safer technology.

Israel had already penetrated the replacement.

Asadi is acknowledging a structural crisis the Islamic Republic has failed to solve: modern life continuously generates data, and the regime cannot know which cameras, networks, databases, suppliers or officers have been compromised.

The Islamic Republic created a surveillance state to ensure that ordinary Iranians could never hide from it.

Now its own commanders admit that they cannot hide from Israel.

2. Attacks around Hormuz are continuing. Iran says six tankers have caught fire after striking mines since Sunday, while UKMTO separately reported a vessel hit by a projectile while transiting outbound through the strait. No casualties were reported in that incident.

3. The Bahrain front remains active too. Iran launched six drones toward a US-linked military site over the weekend, while Bahrain says the attack was intercepted. It was the second such attempt in three days.

4. Diplomacy has not disappeared, but the rhetoric is hardening. Iran continues to say a deal remains possible through Qatari mediation, while Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi warned Tehran may not wait for the US to strike first if it believes another attack is being prepared.

Sovereignty to the Iranian People

ما، جمعی از ۱۰۰ ایرانی پادشاهی‌خواه، با این نامه خواهان پایان سیاست مماشات با جمهوری اسلامی و اتخاذ رویکردی روشن در حمایت از آزادی و حاکمیت ملی مردم ایران هستیم.

جمهوری اسلامی طی نزدیک به پنج دهه نشان داده است که نه اصلاح‌پذیر است و نه اراده‌ای برای تغییر ماهیت سرکوبگر خود دارد. ساختار این حکومت بر سرکوب داخلی، صدور بحران، تهدید امنیت منطقه و تقابل با نظم و امنیت بین‌المللی استوار است.

منشأ بخش بزرگی از ناامنی، بحران و بی‌ثباتی منطقه، سیاست‌های جمهوری اسلامی است. آزادی و امنیت پایدار جهان، بدون رهایی ایران از حاکمیت این نظام، دست‌یافتنی نخواهد بود.

ما از دولت‌های شما مطالبات مشخصی داریم:

۱. پایان مماشات: سیاست مماشات و امتیازدهی به جمهوری اسلامی را متوقف کنید و در برابر سرکوب مردم ایران موضعی قاطع اتخاذ کنید.

۲. به‌رسمیت‌شناختن رضا پهلوی: ایشان را به‌عنوان چهره محوری اپوزیسیون پادشاهی‌خواه و نماینده سیاسی جریان پادشاهی‌خواه ایران در تعاملات سیاسی خود به رسمیت بشناسید.

۳. تحویل سفارتخانه‌های جمهوری اسلامی: از مشروعیت‌بخشی به نمایندگی‌های حکومتی جمهوری اسلامی خودداری کنید و زمینه انتقال مدیریت و کنترل نمایندگی‌های دیپلماتیک ایران در خارج از کشور به نمایندگان مورد تأیید مردم ایران و دفتر شاهزاده رضا پهلوی را، در چارچوب حقوق بین‌الملل، فراهم آورید.

۴. حمایت از گذار: از برنامه‌های دوران گذار و تلاش‌های سازمان‌یافته برای انتقال مسالمت‌آمیز قدرت به مردم ایران حمایت کنید.

۵. حمایت از مردم ایران: برای توقف اعدام‌ها، آزادی زندانیان سیاسی، مقابله با سرکوب و دسترسی آزاد ایرانیان به اینترنت اقدام عملی کنید.

۶. احترام به تمامیت ارضی ایران: از حق مردم ایران برای تعیین نظام سیاسی آینده کشورشان، از طریق انتخاباتی آزاد و دموکراتیک، حمایت کنید.

ما خواهان ایرانی آزاد، سکولار، یکپارچه و آباد هستیم؛ ایرانی که در آن پادشاهی پهلوی می‌تواند با رأی آزاد مردم به نظام سیاسی کشور تبدیل شود.

ما باور داریم پیوند ملت ایران با رضاشاه دوم پهلوی و آرمان بازگشت به حاکمیت ملی، یکی از مسیرهای سیاسی مورد حمایت بخش بزرگی از جامعه پادشاهی‌خواه ایران است.

این نامه درخواست دخالت در تعیین سرنوشت ایران نیست؛ درخواست احترام به حق تعیین سرنوشت ایرانیان است.

از شما می‌خواهیم تاریخ را از دریچه منافع کوتاه‌مدت سیاسی نبینید. ایران آزاد، نه تهدیدی برای جهان، بلکه فرصتی برای صلح، ثبات و همکاری بین‌المللی خواهد بود.

Joint Statement and Urgent Appeal by Iranian Citizens to the Leaders of Democratic Nations

Subject: Ending Appeasement of the Islamic Republic, Recognizing Reza Shah II Pahlavi, and Supporting the Transfer of Sovereignty to the Iranian People

We, a group of 100 Iranian monarchists, call through this letter for an end to the policy of appeasement toward the Islamic Republic and for a clear approach in support of the freedom and national sovereignty of the Iranian people.

Over nearly five decades the Islamic Republic has shown that it is neither reformable nor willing to change its repressive nature. The structure of this regime rests on domestic repression, exporting crises, threatening regional security and confronting international order and security.

A large part of the insecurity, crisis and instability in the region originates in the policies of the Islamic Republic. Lasting freedom and security in the world will not be achievable without freeing Iran from the rule of this system.

We have concrete demands of your governments:

1. End appeasement: stop the policy of appeasement and concessions to the Islamic Republic and take a firm stance against the repression of the Iranian people.

2. Recognise Reza Pahlavi: recognise him in your political engagements as the central figure of the monarchist opposition and the political representative of Iran's monarchist movement.

3. Hand over the Islamic Republic's embassies: refrain from legitimising the regime's diplomatic missions, and, within the framework of international law, prepare the ground for transferring the management and control of Iran's diplomatic missions abroad to representatives approved by the Iranian people and the office of Prince Reza Pahlavi.

4. Support the transition: support transition-period plans and organised efforts for a peaceful transfer of power to the Iranian people.

5. Support the Iranian people: take practical action to stop executions, free political prisoners, counter repression and secure Iranians' free access to the internet.

6. Respect Iran's territorial integrity: support the right of the Iranian people to determine the future political system of their country through free and democratic elections.
